'''Leslie Ann Kolodziejski''' (born July 31, 1958) is an American professor of electrical engineering at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]]. She works on fabricating novel photonic devices after synthesizing the constituent material via [[molecular-beam epitaxy]]. She is a recipient of the [[Presidential Young Investigator Award]] from the [[National Science Foundation]] and is a fellow of [[The Optical Society]].

== Early life and education ==
Kolodziejski earned her undergraduate and graduate degrees at [[Purdue University]], completing her bachelor's degree in 1983 and Master's in 1984.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://engineering.purdue.edu/MSE/people/alumni/awards/alumni-at-universities|title=Alumni with University Careers|website=Materials Engineering - [[Purdue University]]|language=en|access-date=2019-04-30}}</ref> She received her Ph.D. from [[Purdue University]] in 1986, where she worked on [[molecular-beam epitaxy]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kolodziejski|first1=L. A.|last2=Bonsett|first2=T. C.|last3=Gunshor|first3=R. L.|last4=Datta|first4=S.|last5=Bylsma|first5=R. B.|last6=Becker|first6=W. M.|last7=Otsuka|first7=N.|date=1984-08-15|title=Molecular beam epitaxy of diluted magnetic semiconductor (Cd1−xMnxTe) superlattices|journal=[[Applied Physics Letters]]|volume=45|issue=4|pages=440–442|doi=10.1063/1.95223|issn=0003-6951|bibcode=1984ApPhL..45..440K}}</ref><ref name="MedicineEngineering2007">{{cite book|author1=Institute of Medicine|author2-link=National Academy of Engineering|author2=National Academy of Engineering|author3-link=National Academy of Sciences|author3=National Academy of Sciences|title=Advanced Research Instrumentation and Facilities|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=xgpSAgAAQBAJ&pg=PA103|date=28 January 2007|publisher=[[National Academies Press]]|isbn=978-0-309-09701-7|page=103|author1-link=National Academy of Medicine}}</ref>

== Research and career ==
Kolodziejski joined the Electrical and Computer Engineering Department at [[Purdue University]] as an assistant professor in 1986.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.rle.mit.edu/people/directory/leslie-kolodziejski/|title=General Staff Directory {{!}} RLE at MIT|website=[[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]]|access-date=2019-04-30}}</ref> She was awarded the [[National Science Foundation]] [[Presidential Young Investigator Award]] from 1987 to 1993 for researching potential uses of [[molecular-beam epitaxy]] with photo-excitation, for designing more efficient [[Doping (semiconductor)|doping]] processes of [[zinc selenide]] and for studying the resulting product's properties.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=8657556|title=NSF Award Search: Award#8657556 - PYI: N-and P-type Doping of ZnSe|website=www.nsf.gov|access-date=2019-05-02}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=8846919|title=NSF Award Search: Award#8846919 - PYI: N-and P-type Doping of ZnSe|website=www.nsf.gov|access-date=2019-05-02}}</ref> A simultaneous [[United States Naval Research Laboratory]] Fellowship was awarded in 1989 to determine the optimum growth parameters for the [[chemical beam epitaxy]] of [[zinc selenide]] and comparing the product specifications with that obtained via molecular beam epitaxy.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nsf.gov/pubs/stis1992/nsf9255/nsf9255.txt?org=ENG|title=NSF 92-55 Directory of Awards, Engineering Directorate|last=|first=|date=|website=[[National Science Foundation]]|access-date=2019-04-30}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://apps.dtic.mil/dtic/tr/fulltext/u2/a213265.pdf|title=Chemical Beam Epitaxy of ZnSe|last=|first=|date=|website=MIT|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190430214659/https://apps.dtic.mil/dtic/tr/fulltext/u2/a213265.pdf|url-status=live|archive-date=April 30, 2019|access-date=2019-04-30}}</ref>

She moved to the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT) in 1988 to continue to work on [[epitaxial deposition]].<ref name="wired">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.wired.com/2000/09/optical-2/|title=Bright Switch|date=September 1, 2000|accessdate=1 May 2019|magazine=[[Wired (magazine)|Wired]]}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://oge.mit.edu/community/committed-to-caring-c2c/leslie-kolodziejski/|title=Leslie Kolodziejski {{!}} Office of Graduate Education|access-date=2019-04-30}}</ref> In 1992, Kolodziejski was appointed to the Karl van Tassel Career Development Chair and in 1993, to the Esther and Harold E. Edgerton Career Development Chair.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eecs.mit.edu/news-events/announcements/kolodziejski-named-soe-capers-and-marion-mcdonald-award|title=Kolodziejski named for SoE Capers and Marion McDonald Award {{!}} MIT EECS|website=www.eecs.mit.edu|access-date=2019-05-01}}</ref> Kolodziejski was made full professor in the faculty of [[electrical engineering and computer science]] (EECS) in 1999, where she currently teaches at both undergraduate and postgraduate level while leading the ''Integrated Photonic Devices and Materials'' Group and the Nanoprecision Deposition Laboratory.<ref name="jeff" /><ref name=":4">{{Cite web|url=https://news.mit.edu/2011/new-eecs-leadership|title=EECS head Chandrakasan announces new leadership team|website=MIT News|date=14 July 2011 |access-date=2019-04-30}}</ref>

=== Academic service ===
Kolodziejski has served on the editorial boards of ''[[Applied Physics Letters]]'' and the ''[[Journal of Applied Physics]]''.<ref name=":4" /> She is a member of the Truth Values Community, which looks to create a better community for women graduate students at [[MIT]] through a pairing of science and arts.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.truthvaluescommunity.com/our-community|title=The People of Truth Values Community|website=Truth Values Community|language=en-US|access-date=2019-04-30}}</ref> She is also the founder of Leaders in Life, an organization which works to foster leadership among women graduate students.<ref name="jeff">{{cite web |title=Women in Science and Engineering Workshop |url=https://www.jlab.org/conferences/wsw09/bios.html |website=[[Thomas Jefferson National Accelerator Facility]] |accessdate=1 May 2019 |date=November 16, 2009}}</ref>

In 2015, Kolodziejski was awarded an [[Alfred P. Sloan Foundation]] award to create a University Centre of Exemplary Mentoring.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.mit.edu/2015/sloan-foundation-awards-university-center-exemplary-mentoring-grant-0401|title=Alfred P. Sloan Foundation awards grant to create a University Center of Exemplary Mentoring at MIT|website=MIT News|date=April 2015 |access-date=2019-04-30}}</ref> She is also a mentor for the Minority PhD program (MPhD).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://risingstars18-eecs.mit.edu/speaker-kolodziejski/|title=Leslie Kolodziejski|last=Kernis|first=Rachida|website=EECS Rising Stars 2018|language=en-US|access-date=2019-04-30}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://sloanphds.org/mphd.html|title=Alfred P. Sloan Foundation|website=sloanphds.org|access-date=2019-04-30}}</ref>

=== Awards and honors ===
In 2011, Kolodziejski was elected as a fellow of [[The Optical Society]].<ref name=":4" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.osa.org/en-us/awards_and_grants/fellow_members/recent_fellows/2011_fellows/|title=OSA Fellows 2011|last=|first=|date=|website=[[The Optical Society]]|access-date=2019-05-01}}</ref> She was the recipient of the Faculty Ambassador Award, which recognizes "enhancing the experience for students at MIT that transcends the boundaries of the classroom" as well as enthusiastic support for [[multiculturalism]] and [[Diversity (politics)|diversity]].<ref>{{cite web |title=UCEM Leaders win MIT Diversity Awards |url=https://sloan.org/about/news-detail/3691 |website=[[Alfred P. Sloan Foundation]] |accessdate=1 May 2019}}</ref> Other awards and recognition include:

* Office of Naval Research, Young Investigator Award
* National Science Foundation, Presidential Young Investigator Award<ref name="MedicineEngineering2007"/>
